summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹987 mn and EBITDA margin reached 39%, with PAT up 87% YoY to ₹350 mn.
summary.overview: Ellenbarrie posted a strong Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations of ₹987 mn (+18% YoY, +13% QoQ), driven mainly by ramp-up of the Kurnool and Uluberia 2 plants. EBITDA rose to ₹387 mn (+21% YoY, +50% QoQ) at a 39% margin, which management attributed mainly to new power-efficient capacity, cost control and higher production rather than argon pricing. PAT of ₹350 mn was helped by lower finance cost and a lower effective tax rate. Management reaffirmed FY27 capex of ₹250 crore and FY28 capex of ₹200 crore, and said the East India 320 TPD on-site plant should start contributing revenue in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 220 TPD North India plant is backed by contracted demand before commissioning, and how will it compete against incumbents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said merchant plants are not pre-contracted; the site is chosen after a micro-market survey, contracting starts 3–4 months before commissioning, and the ramp to 80–90% utilisation takes 18–24 months. Early focus is on customers located near their factories, where the company has a cost advantage, plus new industries in the area.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about argon pricing and whether 38–39% margins are a fair base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects the business to stabilise at 40% or higher EBITDA margin as capacity unfolds, with 39% in Q1 close to that. It said argon pricing had a very limited impact this quarter, and that the margin gain came mainly from newer, more power-efficient capacity and cost control. It described 40% as a longer-term target, not a quarterly guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Which capacities does the ₹450 crore capex relate to, given East India and North India were announced earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹450 crore is for two merchant plants: North India (not yet operational) and West Central India (construction started). Together they are about 450–500 TPD. The entire residual amount of the ₹450 crore goes to these two plants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current utilisation of bulk and on-site capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy plants are fully utilised. The plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 has some spare capacity. Apart from that, management said nearly all capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: What drove cost discipline and how will costs evolve, particularly power?
qa_highlights.answer: Power is the largest cost. Management cited newer, more efficient plants that use less power per unit of gas, plus one long-term renewable PPA signed, exchange purchases, and ongoing scouting for more long-term PPAs. Other costs such as employee and other expenses were described as having standard annual increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback on a merchant ASU, and what is the margin profile of electronic gases versus ASU-based business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a payback of about 18 months to build, 18–24 months to ramp, then about three years, which an analyst summed to roughly five years excluding construction. For electronic gases, management said margins would be lower than an ASU model because the business is largely import-and-supply trading with limited value addition, though investment is lower than for an ASU.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance reaffirmed at 2,500 million (₹250 crore); FY28 capex guidance 2,000 million (₹200 crore), with ₹450 crore total cited as going to merchant plants.
East India on-site plant of 320 TPD under commissioning; revenue expected in Q2 FY27 (current quarter), per management.
North India merchant plant of 220 TPD not yet operational; construction timing not specified on the call beyond the residual capex going to it.
West Central India ASU merchant plant under construction; together with North India, the two merchant plants total about 450–500 TPD. Plant produces liquid oxygen, nitrogen and argon.
Recently commissioned plant (commissioned Q4 FY26) has some spare capacity; legacy plants described as fully utilised; Kurnool and Uluberia 2 ramp-up ongoing.

Merchant plants assumed to take 18–24 months to ramp to 80–90% utilisation; contracting begins about 3–4 months before commissioning; payback described as 18 months build + 18–24 months ramp + about three years.
Management said plants of 1,000+ TPD would be on-site only; multiple inquiries above 600 TPD are being worked on, and the 600 TPD is the current largest plant.
demand_pricing: Revenue from gases and related products and services ₹973 mn, up 20% YoY and 13% QoQ, driven by volume ramp-up of merchant plants; core gases segment margin 38%.
Oxygen and nitrogen prices stable and largely contractual over the long term; argon prices recovering with a modest sequential increase but still below H1 FY26 levels, per management.

Argon treated as a byproduct of oxygen production; management said argon demand is driven by specialty steel, fabrication, solar cell manufacturing and high-end manufacturing; more argon capacity being moved into longer-term contracts.
Management said current argon prices are 'in the middle' of the long-term trend line, neither significantly boosting nor depressing margins; also said prices are quite above the 200-day DMA.

On-site revenue about ₹14 crore and bulk about ₹70 crore per Q1 investor presentation (as cited by management), so on-site is about 20% of revenue; steel about one-third of revenue and non-steel about two-thirds.
New merchant capacity is not pre-contracted; management said it targets customers near their factories for a cost advantage and greenfield demand from new industries.

Electronic gases: management said these are largely imported, debottled and warehoused, so EBITDA margin would be lower than an ASU model; investment in containers, debulking and health and safety infrastructure.
